annotation.title_clean: Ethical Considerations of Applying Robots in Kindergarten Settings: Towards an Approach from a Macroperspective
annotation.title_en: Ethical Considerations of Applying Robots in Kindergarten Settings: Towards an Approach from a Macroperspective
annotation.authors_or_issuer: Tolksdorf, N.F.; Siebert, S.; Zorn, I.; Horwath, I.; Rohlfing, K.J.
annotation.summary_en: Peer-reviewed article arguing that child–robot interaction research in kindergartens needs a macroperspective on ethics, beyond individual-child effects. It analyses four areas: the kindergarten as institution, children as a vulnerable group, caregivers' role, and pedagogical concepts. It offers a framework for more systematic ethical approaches to cHRI studies.
key_provisions_or_claims: cHRI methodology is limited to a microperspective; a macroperspective on institutional impact is needed.
Children are a vulnerable group, more likely than adults to follow robots' suggestions and form attachments.
Robots entering a kindergarten alter distribution of responsibilities and roles among educators, parents and children.
Four analysed areas: institutional setting, vulnerable children, caregivers' role, pedagogical concepts.
Recommends enhanced warm-ups and adapting study procedures to usual kindergarten activities to reduce disruption.
